neighbours.label: the slot right before a person's reported response in a survey or study frame ('participants were asked to …', 'how customers feel'), predicting an evaluation verb such as 'rate', as against 'to' and 'how' clauses about non-human processes or movement
fire: During the trial, each child was asked to describe the picture in their own words.
In the survey, residents were asked to score the park on cleanliness and safety.
Our page lets you see how guests feel about their stay at each resort.
For the experiment, students were asked to judge the length of two lines.
The pollsters asked about two thousand voters to grade the new mayor.
Check the forum to learn how owners feel about the latest model.
After lunch, the panel of tasters was asked to evaluate six cheeses.
A short form invited visitors to rank the exhibits from best to worst.
quiet: During the trip, each child walked to the bus stop with a teacher.
In the spring, residents went to the park to plant new trees.
Our page lets you see how the tides change along the coast each month.
For the experiment, the samples were heated to the boiling point.
The pollsters drove about two hundred miles to reach the new office.

predictions: 6/8 fire 0.2-0.5 on 'to' or the human noun; near misses below 0.1
notes: Probes: 'asked to rate' 0.444 but 'asked to walk' also 0.444 (fires before the verb, so the frame matters, not the verb); 'how customers feel' 0.543 vs 'how the engine works' 0.021; 'patients rate' 0.033 (fires before, not on, 'rate'). Near misses keep 'to'/'how' but drop the elicitation frame.
